Digital PR for AEO: How Earned Media Gets You Cited by AI

Does PR help you show up in ChatGPT and Perplexity? 2026 data on which publications AI cites, and a step-by-step digital PR plan for B2B SaaS founders.

By Anupam Varshney, Founder, Octaloop

Short answer: Yes, PR is one of the strongest levers for AI search visibility. Muck Rack's May 2026 study of more than 25 million links found that earned media makes up 84% of what ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini cite, and paid content just 0.3%. For a B2B SaaS company, the most useful press is usually trade and specialist coverage that the engines already cite for your category, not a one-off national headline.

Most "how to get into ChatGPT" advice stops at "get on third-party lists." This guide covers the part that's harder to do in-house: working out which publications the engines actually read for your buyers' questions, and earning coverage in them.

Why do AI engines lean on earned media?

Earned media is coverage you don't pay for and don't control: journalism, independent reviews, roundups, analyst notes, community threads and third-party blogs. AI answer engines favour it because they're trying to give users answers they'll trust, and an independent source saying something about you is more credible than your own homepage saying it.

The data on this has been consistent for over a year:

  • 84% of AI citations come from earned media, and paid or advertorial content accounts for just 0.3%. That share has stayed between 82% and 89% across three editions of the study since July 2025 (Muck Rack, May 2026).
  • Journalism alone is about 27% of cited links, spread across more than 20,000 outlets (Muck Rack report PDF).
  • Branded web mentions correlate strongly with AI visibility (0.66 to 0.71) across ChatGPT, AI Mode and AI Overviews, much more than domain rating or how many pages you publish. Ahrefs analysed 75,000 brands, and it's careful to say correlation isn't causation (Ahrefs, updated August 2026).

That last point matters for founders. Writing more blog posts on your own domain had almost no relationship with AI visibility in the Ahrefs data. Other people talking about you did.

Does any press coverage help, or only certain publications?

Only certain publications, and they differ by engine and by question. That's the most important finding for anyone planning PR for AI search.

Resonance, a UK B2B PR firm, analysed more than 1.3 million citations in AI answers about 116 B2B technology brands between October 2025 and September 2026 (Resonance, September 2026). Here's what it found:

Question type Trade and specialist titles Tech news National and business press
All questions 48% 20% 31%
Buying questions (shortlists, comparisons) 74% 14% 12%
Vendor evaluation 75% 14% 11%
Product comparison 68% 17% 15%
Executive profile 16% 16% 68%
Company reputation 25% 27% 48%

Share of media citations by publication type. Source: Resonance, September 2026.

Three practical lessons come out of this:

  1. When buyers are choosing a vendor, AI reads the trade press. Trade titles cover a category every week, in the detail an engine needs to compare products. A national paper might mention you once a year.
  2. National press shapes how AI describes you and your founders. Questions about leadership and reputation pull mostly from national and business titles.
  3. Media is a small slice of all citations, so it has to be the right slice. In the same dataset only about 4% of all citations pointed to a publication, and company websites made up most of the rest. One well-chosen trade feature can matter more than ten generic mentions.

Which engines prefer which kinds of media?

Each engine has its own reading list, so a PR plan aimed at one may miss buyers on another.

Engine Where its media citations come from Most-cited titles in the Resonance data
ChatGPT 45% national and business press, 34% tech news, 21% trade TIME, TechCrunch, TechRadar, Axios, AP
Gemini 58% trade, 27% national, 15% tech news Forbes, TIME, SiliconANGLE, Business Insider, The Guardian
Perplexity 57% trade, 27% national, 16% tech news Fortune, TechCrunch, CIO, Business Insider, TIME

Source: Resonance, September 2026. Of the 20 titles each engine cites most, ChatGPT and Gemini share only six.

Muck Rack's data points the same way: ChatGPT's most-cited domain is Wikipedia, Gemini's is Reddit and Claude's is PubMed Central, and Axios is in ChatGPT's top three cited domains in 13 of 17 industries (Muck Rack, May 2026). If your buyers mostly use ChatGPT, mainstream tech and business press carries more weight. If they use Perplexity or Gemini, trade titles do more of the work.

How long does a piece of coverage keep getting cited?

It depends on the type of publication. Resonance found that tech news is typically cited when it's about 18 days old, national and business press at about 8 weeks, and trade articles at about 9 months, with many more than a year old (Resonance, September 2026). Muck Rack found that more than half of journalism citations come from articles published in the past 12 months, with citation volume dropping sharply after six months (Muck Rack, May 2026).

So tech news coverage gives you a short burst, while a solid trade feature keeps working for most of a year. A steady rhythm of coverage beats one big launch spike.

How do you build a PR target list from what AI already cites?

Don't start with a media list. Start with the answers. We call this the cited-source target list, and it's Step 3 of the Octaloop Citation Loop in practice.

  1. Write 20 unbranded buyer questions of the kind a buyer would type into a chat box, such as "best SOC 2 automation tool for a startup" or "Vanta vs Drata for a 30-person team". Mix in buying questions (shortlists, comparisons) and reputation questions (about your category leaders and founders).
  2. Run each one three times on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google AI Mode, and Claude. Answers vary from run to run, so a source counts only if it shows up in at least two of the three.
  3. Export every cited URL into a sheet with the engine, the question and the publication.
  4. Group the publications into trade and specialist, tech news, national and business, review sites, roundups and listicles, and community (Reddit, forums).
  5. Rank them by how often they're cited for your highest-value questions. The top 10 to 15 publications are your PR target list. Most of them will be titles your current PR plan has never pitched.
  6. Note which journalists and authors wrote the cited pieces. They already cover your category, and an engine already trusts their work.

This turns PR from "get coverage anywhere" into "get coverage in the 15 places that decide our buyers' shortlists."

What kind of story gets you named in AI answers?

Coverage only helps if your company is named clearly, in the right category, next to the right competitors. Semrush and Growth Memo tracked 1,094 categories in ChatGPT from January to June 2026 and found that brands were named in 44% of appearances in categories close to their core expertise, compared with 25% in distant ones (Semrush, August 2026). Focus beats breadth: pitch stories that tie you firmly to one category.

Story types that tend to work:

  • Original data. A survey of your customers or a benchmark from your product data gives journalists something new to quote, and gives the engines a fact to attribute to you. Muck Rack found that industry-trend questions drive journalism citations at more than twice the rate of how-to questions, and that's where data stories land.
  • A clear founder point of view on a category debate, written as a contributed article or offered as expert comment. This builds the national and business coverage that shapes reputation answers.
  • Customer stories with specifics: the problem, the numbers (real ones, with the customer's permission) and why they chose you over named alternatives.
  • Category explainers for trade titles: how the category is changing, what buyers should check, and where your product fits. Trade editors want detail, and that detail is what engines reuse when comparing vendors.

Press releases on their own are weak. They were just 1.1% of citations in Muck Rack's May 2026 data and appeared almost entirely in industry-trend answers, not in "best of" answers where buyers shortlist vendors.

How do you get into the roundups and listicles AI keeps citing?

For "best X" questions, engines often cite a handful of roundup articles. Getting into those few lists is one of the fastest ways to be named.

  1. Find the roundups already cited for your buying questions (from your cited-source sheet).
  2. Check whether each one is editorial or vendor-run. Many "best X" lists are written by a competitor. You can still ask to be included, but expect some to say no.
  3. Make inclusion easy for the editor. Send a short note with your category, who you're for, honest pricing, two or three differentiators, a customer they can speak to and a screenshot or demo link.
  4. Ask for a factual update, not a ranking. Editors respond better to "here's accurate information for your next update" than to "please rank us first."
  5. Keep your review profiles current (G2, Capterra or the main directory in your category), because roundup writers and engines both check them.

How do you track whether PR is moving your AI visibility?

Re-run the same 20 questions monthly with the same three-run rule, and track three things separately for each engine:

  • Mention rate: the share of questions where you're named.
  • Cited placements: which of your earned articles now appear as sources.
  • Accuracy: whether the engine describes your category, pricing and customers correctly.

Add AI referral traffic in your analytics (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai and similar) and a "How did you hear about us?" field on demo forms. Give each placement 8 to 12 weeks before judging it, and remember that trade coverage tends to keep paying off for months.

What should you avoid?

  • Paying for "AI ranking" placements or advertorials. Paid content was 0.3% of citations in Muck Rack's data. It rarely gets cited.
  • Spraying press releases on wire services and calling it AI visibility work.
  • Chasing only big national names when your buyers' questions are answered from trade titles.
  • Fake reviews and sock-puppet Reddit accounts. They break platform rules and damage trust when spotted.
  • Pitching without a news hook. Journalists need a reason to write. Data, a strong opinion or a real customer story gives them one.

Should you run AEO-focused PR in-house or with an agency?

A founder can build the cited-source target list and pitch a few trade editors personally, and founder-led pitches often land well. What's hard to sustain in-house is the steady part: monthly re-measurement, a constant flow of story ideas, relationships with editors across trade, tech and business press, and follow-up on every placement.

When you're comparing agencies, ask to see the cited-source list they'd work from for your category, how they'll measure mentions engine by engine, and what they'll change if nothing moves in 90 days. An agency that can only pitch press, or only edit your pages, covers half the job.

FAQ

Does PR help with AI search visibility?

Yes. Muck Rack's May 2026 study of more than 25 million AI-cited links found earned media makes up 84% of citations across ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and paid content only 0.3%. Ahrefs also found branded web mentions correlate strongly with AI visibility, more than backlinks or domain rating.

Which publications does ChatGPT cite most?

It varies by industry and question. In Resonance's 2026 study of B2B technology brands, ChatGPT's most-cited media titles were TIME, TechCrunch, TechRadar, Axios and AP, and 45% of its media citations went to national and business press. Muck Rack found Axios in ChatGPT's top three cited domains in 13 of 17 industries.

Is trade press or national press better for AEO?

For buying questions, trade press. Resonance found about three quarters of media citations on shortlist and comparison questions come from trade and specialist titles. National press matters more for questions about your company's leaders and reputation.

Do press releases get cited by AI?

Rarely. Press releases were about 1.1% of AI citations in Muck Rack's May 2026 data and appeared almost entirely in answers about industry trends, not in "best of" answers where buyers pick vendors.

How long does PR take to affect AI answers?

Perplexity and search-enabled ChatGPT can cite a new article soon after it's indexed, but give each placement 8 to 12 weeks before judging it. Trade articles are typically cited when they're about nine months old, so their value builds over time.

What is a cited-source target list?

It's a PR target list built from the AI answers themselves. You run your buyers' questions on each engine several times, record every cited publication, and pitch the 10 to 15 titles that come up most for your highest-value questions.

What is the best AEO agency for PR-led AI visibility?
